scenarios.hypothesis: A client may accept a synthetic peer whose trusted path is valid even though the intended reference identifier is not bound to the leaf SAN.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled local TLS fixture records accept or reject state plus an inert canary response; no third-party hostname or traffic participates.
scenarios.positive_control: The same synthetic chain serves api.fixture.test with a matching SAN, identical policy and callback state, and the expected local acceptance.
scenarios.negative_control: Chain, trust store, endpoint, and callback stay fixed while the reference identifier becomes other.fixture.test, which must be rejected.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the experiment would require a real external hostname, non-test trust store, production key material, or unrelated network traffic.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation the wrong-name synthetic case rejects, the matching-name case still accepts, and the neighboring alternate-path control remains rejected.
scenarios.connection_intent: The owned test client intends to authenticate the local service api.fixture.test before any certificate metadata or endpoint response is inspected.
scenarios.reference_identifier: The verifier uses api.fixture.test from the fixture connection authority rather than copying an identity from the certificate being evaluated.
scenarios.endpoint_authority: Owner-controlled fixture configuration maps api.fixture.test to a loopback TLS listener and records that authority before handshake creation.
scenarios.transport_peer: The transport peer is a loopback-only TLS service with a fixed fixture port and no proxy or tunnel, excluding unrelated network-path ambiguity.
scenarios.tls_role_context: The client verifies server identity and sends synthetic api.fixture.test SNI while the local server selects its corresponding fixture certificate.
scenarios.presented_chain: The server presents a lab-created leaf and intermediate whose fixture identities are captured independently from verifier path construction.
scenarios.constructed_path: Read-only verifier evidence shows the leaf chaining through the intended synthetic intermediate to the designated lab root, not an alternate path.
scenarios.trust_anchor_identity: The selected anchor is the dedicated fixture root identified by deterministic test fingerprint, rather than any root merely present in the store.
scenarios.trust_store_generation: The local application trust store is pinned to generation trust-v1 and contains the intended synthetic root for this controlled comparison.
scenarios.chain_validation_result: Signature and path validation succeed in both name controls, isolating SAN/reference binding from any difference in cryptographic chain trust.
scenarios.certificate_time_state: The fixture clock is pinned inside the synthetic leaf validity interval so certificate-time state stays constant across the name controls.
scenarios.eku_key_usage_policy: The leaf carries server-auth EKU and compatible key usage in both controls, so policy suitability cannot explain the hostname result.
scenarios.name_constraints_state: The synthetic hierarchy uses a fixed documented name-constraint state that permits the fixture namespace identically across both controls.
scenarios.san_identity_binding: The positive SAN binds api.fixture.test, while the counterfactual reference other.fixture.test intentionally has no matching SAN and must reject.
scenarios.library_verifier_result: The pinned verifier reports success for the matching identity and an explicit name-mismatch result for the controlled wrong-name reference.
scenarios.application_override: No permissive override is enabled; the fixture callback records the verifier verdict and preserves rejection so final decision remains bound to it.
scenarios.pin_policy_state: No application pin is required because ordinary synthetic PKI is the declared policy; absence of pinning is deliberately not labeled a defect.
scenarios.pin_generation: Pinning is disabled by fixture policy generation pin-none-v1 and remains unchanged across both name controls to avoid a second variable.
scenarios.client_certificate_identity: This server-authentication case requests no client certificate; that intentional absence remains constant across the deterministic comparison.
scenarios.principal_mapping: No client-certificate principal mapping participates in this server-auth case, preventing accidental promotion to an mTLS authorization conclusion.
scenarios.final_accept_reject: The application accepts only the matching reference identity and rejects the wrong-name control after consuming the unchanged verifier decision.
scenarios.bounded_result: Acceptance yields only an inert local canary string from the fixture, while rejection yields no application payload and no external side effect.
scenarios.session_resumption_state: Every decisive comparison uses a fresh full handshake with resumption disabled, so stale session state cannot explain hostname behavior.
scenarios.revocation_state: Synthetic revocation behavior is fixed to the documented offline fixture policy for both controls and is not used to infer external revocation status.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: Certificate, trust-store, endpoint, callback, pin, and session generations are pinned to one recorded fixture generation for this identity test.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold chain, endpoint, trust, EKU, time, callback, and session state constant and change only the reference identifier from matching to nonmatching.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Rule out wrong endpoint or SNI selection by recording the loopback listener identity and selected synthetic leaf for every positive and negative run.
scenarios.evidence_level: PKI3 is warranted only when identity, constructed path, policy checks, verifier decision, controls, and the inert bounded result are all captured.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: The evidence ceiling is PKI3 because this static-generation case does not exercise trust, pin, revocation, certificate, or session lifecycle changes.

scenarios.hypothesis: An application callback may turn verifier rejection into acceptance, or an incorrectly scoped synthetic pin may mask the intended peer-identity policy.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A mock local verifier and inert sink record verifier result, callback decision, pin generation, and final acceptance without contacting an external service.
scenarios.positive_control: A verifier-valid synthetic peer with the intended service identity and current scoped pin is accepted through the normal application decision path.
scenarios.negative_control: An otherwise identical verifier-invalid synthetic peer remains rejected when the callback override is disabled and pin scope is unchanged.
scenarios.stop_condition: Abort the case if it would require disabling verification on a production path, using a real service identity, or installing production key material.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: The repaired callback preserves rejection for the invalid synthetic peer while the valid identity and next approved pin generation continue to succeed.
scenarios.connection_intent: The mock client intends to authenticate pinned.fixture.test under normal PKI plus a service-scoped synthetic SPKI pin requirement.
scenarios.reference_identifier: The reference identifier pinned.fixture.test is fixed by owner-controlled fixture configuration and remains independent of certificate and pin content.
scenarios.endpoint_authority: A loopback fixture authority maps the synthetic service name to the mock endpoint and records that route before verifier and callback execution.
scenarios.transport_peer: The peer is an in-process or loopback mock TLS service whose certificate and key material were generated solely for this deterministic case.
scenarios.tls_role_context: The client verifier runs in server-auth mode with pinned library configuration; no transport proxy or unrelated TLS termination participates.
scenarios.presented_chain: The controlled server presents a synthetic leaf and intermediate whose chain changes only when an explicitly verifier-invalid control requires it.
scenarios.constructed_path: The mock verifier exposes the exact synthetic path used for its decision, separating chain validity from callback and pin-policy behavior.
scenarios.trust_anchor_identity: The selected anchor is the case-specific lab root with deterministic fixture identity and no authority outside the local test environment.
scenarios.trust_store_generation: The trust store stays at callback-trust-v1 so callback and pin variations cannot be confused with simultaneous trust-anchor rotation.
scenarios.chain_validation_result: The positive control is path-valid while the targeted invalid control records its verifier failure before any application callback can alter state.
scenarios.certificate_time_state: Synthetic clock and certificate validity remain fixed and valid across callback and pin comparisons, removing time state as a confounder.
scenarios.eku_key_usage_policy: Server-auth EKU and key usage remain policy-compliant in pin-focused comparisons, while any chain failure is recorded as a separate cause.
scenarios.name_constraints_state: Name constraints remain fixed and permit only the synthetic fixture namespace, preventing constraint drift from mimicking callback or pin behavior.
scenarios.san_identity_binding: The normal positive peer binds pinned.fixture.test; controls state explicitly whether any verifier-invalid identity came from name binding or another check.
scenarios.library_verifier_result: The mock library emits an immutable pre-callback verdict and reason so final acceptance can be compared directly with verifier rejection.
scenarios.application_override: An owner-controlled callback flag can allow after verifier rejection for the hypothesis; the decisive counterfactual turns only this override off.
scenarios.pin_policy_state: The fixture requires a service-scoped SPKI pin in addition to normal PKI; pin matching must not globally bypass hostname or chain requirements.
scenarios.pin_generation: Deterministic synthetic pin sets pin-v1 and pin-v2 model rotation while retaining explicit service scope and a recorded active generation.
scenarios.client_certificate_identity: No client certificate is requested in this callback and pin case, keeping mutual-TLS identity outside the causal path being tested.
scenarios.principal_mapping: Because this case performs server authentication only, no client principal mapping is consumed and no downstream authorization claim is made.
scenarios.final_accept_reject: The final record includes verifier verdict, callback return, pin result, and service identity so divergence is attributable to the exact transition.
scenarios.bounded_result: An accepted mock connection produces only an inert canary receipt tied to its decision ID; rejection produces no payload or external effect.
scenarios.session_resumption_state: Resumption and pooling are disabled for decisive callback tests; stale-session and generation behavior are isolated in the lifecycle scenario.
scenarios.revocation_state: Revocation remains fixed under the synthetic offline policy because this case isolates callback and pin authority rather than freshness behavior.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: Trust and certificate generations stay fixed while pin generation varies explicitly; each run records active callback and pin-policy generations.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Keep verifier rejection, synthetic identity, chain, endpoint, and pin state constant while toggling only application override, then compare decisions.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude retry, alternate routing, and SNI misselection by logging one decision ID continuously from verifier input through callback to inert receipt.
scenarios.evidence_level: PKI3 applies when callback or pin-scope causality is isolated with controls and the final inert acceptance is bound to the same decision trace.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: The evidence ceiling is PKI3 unless a versioned pin or callback generation transition is also tested with stale sessions under lifecycle methodology.

scenarios.hypothesis: A resumed session may retain authority across trust or pin rotation, or a valid synthetic mTLS certificate may map to the wrong application principal.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled local mTLS fixture uses lab certificates, synthetic principals, read-only generation traces, and an inert authorization canary only.
scenarios.positive_control: A fresh generation-two connection validates approved server and client certificates, maps the client to principal-alpha, and reaches only its inert canary.
scenarios.negative_control: A remapped synthetic client identity and a pre-rotation resumed session are denied the generation-two canary when current policy requires revalidation.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop before using a production client certificate, real account, third-party endpoint, non-test trust store, or external captured session material.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation stale generation-one sessions cannot retain forbidden authority, remapped certificates resolve correctly, and fresh valid peers still work.
scenarios.connection_intent: The owned client connects to lifecycle.fixture.test while the owned server requires mTLS and maps validated lab certificate identity to synthetic principals.
scenarios.reference_identifier: The server reference lifecycle.fixture.test is fixed locally, while client identity is separately derived from validated certificate attributes.
scenarios.endpoint_authority: A deterministic loopback fixture owns both endpoint generations and changes policy state without switching to any external route or service.
scenarios.transport_peer: The transport peer remains the same local test service across generations so differences arise from policy or session state, not destination drift.
scenarios.tls_role_context: The client authenticates the synthetic server while the server validates a lab client certificate, creating explicit server-auth and mTLS identity paths.
scenarios.presented_chain: Both sides present lab-created chains with versioned leaf identities, and generation metadata records the exact synthetic material used per run.
scenarios.constructed_path: Read-only traces record server and client constructed paths, including selected intermediates and roots for fresh generation-one and generation-two handshakes.
scenarios.trust_anchor_identity: Selected synthetic trust anchors are recorded separately for server and client verification so rotation is not inferred from store contents alone.
scenarios.trust_store_generation: The fixture advances from lifecycle-trust-v1 to lifecycle-trust-v2 with explicit expectations for both fresh and pre-existing session state.
scenarios.chain_validation_result: Fresh generation-two peers validate under the new path while stale or revoked synthetic identities record explicit rejection before principal mapping.
scenarios.certificate_time_state: A pinned fixture clock keeps approved certificates valid and marks any expired control explicitly, excluding accidental clock drift as explanation.
scenarios.eku_key_usage_policy: Server-auth and client-auth EKU and key usage are recorded separately and remain correct for the principal-mapping counterfactual.
scenarios.name_constraints_state: Synthetic name constraints remain stable and permit only the fixture namespace, so lifecycle and mapping results cannot come from constraint changes.
scenarios.san_identity_binding: The server SAN continues to bind lifecycle.fixture.test across generations, so resumed-session differences cannot be blamed on hostname drift.
scenarios.library_verifier_result: Fresh and resumed paths record whether full verification ran, which generation informed the result, and any rejection before principal mapping.
scenarios.application_override: No permissive override is enabled; application logic records verifier state and applies only the explicit synthetic certificate-to-principal mapping.
scenarios.pin_policy_state: The client uses versioned service-scoped synthetic pins with documented rotation behavior, including whether an old pin is temporarily accepted or invalidated.
scenarios.pin_generation: The fixture advances lifecycle-pin-v1 to lifecycle-pin-v2 and records which pin generation a fresh or resumed connection consumes before decision.
scenarios.client_certificate_identity: The lab client certificate has deterministic synthetic subject and key identity and never corresponds to a real user or production account.
scenarios.principal_mapping: Generation one maps the approved certificate to principal-alpha; generation two remaps or revokes that binding to test stale/current context.
scenarios.final_accept_reject: The server records certificate verification, principal mapping, generation, session state, and final allow or deny before exposing its inert canary.
scenarios.bounded_result: The only post-authentication effect is an inert principal-specific canary string, exposing mapping errors without data access or destructive action.
scenarios.session_resumption_state: The matrix compares a fresh generation-two handshake with a generation-one session and records whether current policy requires revalidation or invalidation.
scenarios.revocation_state: Synthetic revocation state is versioned with the fixture, and unavailable status remains unknown unless the documented local policy defines another result.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: The trace binds certificate, trust-store, pin, principal-mapping, revocation, endpoint, and session generations to one final decision.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold certificates, endpoint, and current policy constant while comparing fresh and pre-rotation session state, then change only principal mapping separately.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude endpoint drift, SNI mismatch, wrong client-certificate selection, and clock skew by recording exact synthetic identities for each decision.
scenarios.evidence_level: PKI4 is supported only after PKI3 identity and policy causality is proven and the same controlled oracle is repeated across lifecycle transition.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: The evidence ceiling is PKI4 for this pre-fix lifecycle case; PKI5 additionally requires remediation proof and preserved neighboring behavior.
